adv.title: Advantages you'll feel.
adv1.p: A beautiful site that brings no leads is just an expensive picture. We design every page around one goal: turning a visitor into a client.
adv1.list: We arrange blocks to lead visitors from the first screen to your lead form.
Buttons and forms sit right where the customer wants to buy.
We optimize images, fonts and code so nobody leaves while waiting.
We set up analytics with goals so you can see where leads come from.
adv2.p: Want to work with clients from other countries? We'll build your site in several languages from day one — just like the one you're reading now.
adv2.list: An easy language picker that remembers each visitor's choice.
The site opens in the language of the visitor's browser.
We tailor the text to each language instead of just running it through a translator.
Separate titles and descriptions so your site gets found in search across countries.
adv3.p: You pay for concrete results, not big words. We calculate the cost honestly and up front.
adv3.list: Before we start, we spell out what makes up the price.
The price doesn't change along the way unless the scope does.
You work directly with us — no agency markup.
Pay in parts as the project progresses.
adv4.p: We work with clients from any country and accept payment in the currency that suits you.
adv4.list: We invoice in whichever currency is convenient for you.
Card transfer, invoice payment or via freelance marketplaces.
We adapt to your schedule for calls and discussions.
Telegram, email or video call — whatever works best for you.
adv5.p: We don't vanish after handoff. A site has to keep working — and we stand behind that.
adv5.list: We fix any bugs found after launch for free.
For the first month after delivery, we help with edits and questions at no charge.
We show you how to update text and images on the site yourself.
We can keep improving and maintaining your site long term.
process.title: Five steps to launch.
p1.p: We hop on a call and dig into your goals, audience and competitors. We set the timeline and budget — free of charge.
p2.p: We map out page structure and the user journey. You see how the site will work before any design begins.
p3.p: We craft a unique look for your brand and get your approval on every screen.
p4.p: We code it, build it and bring it to life with animations. You see progress every 2–3 days.
p5.p: We check it on phones, tablets and across browsers — then we launch.
team.title: A small team.
team.text: There are two of us — and that's a plus. You talk directly to the people building your site: no managers, no game of telephone, no agency markup.
team1.d: Owns how the site looks and feels: structure, visuals, animations.
team2.d: Owns how the site works: code, forms, speed, publishing and support.
reviews.title: Clients will tell.
r1.q: Our first client's review will appear here. Maybe yours?
r2.q: A spot for a review of your landing page, promo site or event website.
r3.q: We're just starting to collect reviews — and each one is worth its weight in gold to us.
faq.title: Questions and answers.
faq.text: Didn't find your answer? Message us — we'll reply within a couple of hours.
q1: Do you only do the design, or the whole website?
a1: The whole thing: design, front-end, programming and launch. You get a finished, working site, not just a mockup.
q2: How long does a project take?
a2: From 3–7 days for a business card site to 20–30 days for a portal. We give an exact timeline after a short brief.
q3: How much does a website cost?
a3: From $500. The price depends on the scope of work. We lock it in before we start and don't change it unless the scope changes.
q4: What do you need from us to start?
a4: A short brief: what your business is, who the site is for and which sites you like. Texts and photos if you have them; if not, we'll help.
q5: Can the site be in several languages?
a5: Yes. This site is the example: five languages with a switcher and browser language auto-detection.
a6: A month of free support, a warranty on bugs and training on managing your site. After that, we can keep maintaining the project.
a7: In stages and in a currency that suits you: card transfer, invoice payment or via freelance marketplaces.
